A marathon is 26.2 miles (42.195 kilometers).

This distance was standardized at the 1908 London Olympics, where the course was set from Windsor Castle to the Olympic stadium, with the finish line in front of the royal box. It became the official standard in 1921.

Fun fact: the race is named after the legend of Pheidippides, a Greek messenger who supposedly ran from the Battle of Marathon to Athens (about 25 miles) to announce the Greek victory over the Persians.
